title: What Are Chatbots and How They Help Tourism Agencies
description: Learn what chatbots are, how they work in the tourism industry, and how they can transform customer support for your travel agency.
content:
What Are Chatbots?

Chatbots are software programs that use artificial intelligence to conduct conversations with users through text or voice interfaces. In tourism, chatbots serve as virtual assistants that can answer guest inquiries, assist with bookings, and provide destination information — all 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.

According to Juniper Research, chatbots have saved the tourism industry over $8 billion annually by 2025, and that number continues to grow. For travel agencies in Croatia, particularly those operating in Dalmatia, chatbots represent a critical technology for competing in the global market.

How Do Chatbots Work in Tourism?

Modern tourism chatbots use advanced AI models that understand natural language. This means a guest can ask a question in their own language — whether it is English, German, Italian, or any other — and receive a relevant response within seconds.

Here is how a typical tourism chatbot works in practice:

  • Intent recognition — The chatbot analyzes the user's message and determines what they want (booking, information, complaint)
  • Query processing — The system searches the database for activities, prices, availability, and other relevant information
  • Response generation — AI composes a personalized response tailored to the conversation context
  • Continuous learning — Every interaction improves the quality of future responses

5 Key Benefits of Chatbots for Travel Agencies

1. 24/7 Availability Without Additional Costs

Tourists often plan trips outside agency business hours. A chatbot can receive an inquiry at 11 PM and immediately provide an answer, while traditional support would require a night shift. For an agency working with guests from different time zones, this is invaluable.

2. Multilingual Support

Croatia attracts guests from all over Europe and the world. An AI chatbot can communicate in 50+ languages without the need to hire translators. A German tourist can ask about a trip to Brac in their language, while a French visitor simultaneously requests information about kayaking in Split.

3. Instant Bookings and Confirmations

A chatbot can guide users through the entire booking process — from selecting an activity to payment — without waiting for an agent's response. Studies show that every minute of waiting reduces conversion probability by 7%.

4. Personalized Recommendations

Based on guest preferences, the chatbot can suggest activities that best match their profile. A family with children will receive different suggestions than a couple looking for a romantic outing or a group of friends seeking adrenaline.

5. Reduced Employee Workload

Up to 80% of inquiries agencies receive are repetitive questions: "How much does it cost?", "What is included?", "How do I get to the starting point?" The chatbot handles these routine inquiries, while employees can focus on more complex requests and building client relationships.

Chatbots in Practice: Tourism Examples

Major travel platforms like Booking.com and Expedia have been using chatbots for customer support for years. However, this technology is no longer reserved only for big players.

Smaller travel agencies in Dalmatia can implement a chatbot that:

  • Answers questions about available excursions and activities in Split and surroundings
  • Displays prices and availability in real time
  • Guides users through the booking process step by step
  • Sends automatic confirmations and reminders via email
  • Collects feedback after completed activities

One of the key advantages for Croatian agencies is the ability to integrate with local activity management systems, Google Sheets databases, and payment systems.

Statistics That Speak for Themselves

According to 2025 data:

  • 67% of users prefer communicating with a chatbot for simple inquiries
  • Chatbots increase conversion rates by 25-40% in the tourism sector
  • Average chatbot response time is 2-3 seconds, compared to 4-24 hours for email
  • 90% of routine inquiries can be fully automated
  • Agencies with chatbots report 35% higher customer satisfaction

How to Get Started with a Chatbot for Your Agency

Implementing a chatbot does not have to be complicated or expensive. Modern tools like the n8n platform enable creation of sophisticated chatbot systems without the need for programming. The key steps are:

  1. Define objectives — Determine what you want the chatbot to do (support, bookings, recommendations)
  2. Prepare a knowledge base — Gather all information about your services, prices, and policies
  3. Choose a platform — Integrate the chatbot on your website, Telegram, WhatsApp, or Facebook Messenger
  4. Test and optimize — Continuously improve responses based on real interactions
